CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFOBJECT

On ColdFusion for Windows NT, CFOBJECT creates a COM object (Word, Excel, your own ActiveX DLLs), connects to a CORBA server or instantiates a Java class, and you then call its methods and properties from CFML. KoldFusion for UNIX has no COM subsystem and ships without a configured JVM or ORB, so the tag always raises an error of type Object.

Category

Extensibility

Syntax

<CFOBJECT TYPE="COM/CORBA/JAVA"
    ACTION="Create/Connect"
    CLASS="program_id"
    NAME="object_name"
    CONTEXT="InProc/Local/Remote/IOR/NameService"
    SERVER="server_name"
    LOCALE="locale">

Attributes

TYPE
Optional, default "COM". Kind of object: COM, CORBA or JAVA.
ACTION
Required for COM and JAVA. "Create" makes a new object; "Connect" attaches to a running COM server.
CLASS
Required. ProgID of the COM object (for example "Excel.Application"), Java class name, or for CORBA the IOR file name or naming service path.
NAME
Required. Variable that receives the object.
CONTEXT
Optional. COM: InProc, Local or Remote. CORBA: IOR or NameService.
SERVER
Optional. COM server name for CONTEXT="Remote".
LOCALE
Optional. CORBA locale setting.

Usage

Because the tag always fails here, wrap it in CFTRY and catch TYPE="Object" so the page can fall back to something else. CreateObject (new in 4.5) is the function form and behaves the same way.

CFOBJECT can be disabled in the Administrator (Basic Security, Tag Restrictions); a restricted tag raises a security error instead.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- Try to start Excel; on UNIX, plan B is a plain HTML table --->
<CFTRY>
  <CFOBJECT TYPE="COM" ACTION="Create" CLASS="Excel.Application" NAME="Excel">
  <P>Excel is running. Remarkable.</P>
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Object">
    <CFOUTPUT>
    <P><B>No COM today:</B> #CFCATCH.Message#<BR>
    <I>#CFCATCH.Detail#</I></P>
    </CFOUTPUT>
    <CFQUERY NAME="Depts" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
    SELECT Dept_Name, Location FROM Departments ORDER BY Dept_Name
    </CFQUERY>
    <P>Here is the spreadsheet as an HTML table instead:</P>
    <TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
    <CFOUTPUT QUERY="Depts"><TR><TD>#Dept_Name#</TD><TD>#Location#</TD></TR></CFOUTPUT>
    </TABLE>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
